question: Does the 8767 dashboard correctly report more than 170 MB for a VM app, and how does that compare to current memory work?

dashboard.displayCalculation: currentMiB = rssBytes / 1048576, rendered to two decimal places
dashboard.displayUnits: MiB (2^20 bytes); distinct from decimal MB (10^6 bytes)
dashboard.cardCurrentCalculation: Latest saved sampled RSS for this exact source/boot/PID/starttime session
dashboard.cardSampledPeakCalculation: MAX(rss) across all saved session samples, not OS lifetime VmHWM
dashboard.cardAverageCalculation: AVG(rss) across all saved session samples
dashboard.metricWindowLimit: Card current/peak/average stay whole-session values when a chart/recording time window is selected.
dashboard.timestampMeaning: Remote collector sends counters/identity; server time.time() when ingesting records the sample timestamp. UI age reflects server receipt time, not separately transmitted guest capture time.

conclusion.metric: Dashboard current RSS agrees exactly with independent guest VmRSS for all three identified processes. No stale-session, aggregation or units error found.
conclusion.build: All three running guest ELF files directly depend on AWS SDK S3/core, curl and QtNetwork. They predate the lazy-module/native-IPC build structure; their executable hashes differ from the measured current candidate and canonical rebuilt binary. Exact guest source commits remain unknown.
conclusion.kde: 179.22265625 MiB RSS, 66.666015625 MiB PSS, 52.9765625 MiB private. LLVM/Gallium contribute 58.40234375 MiB RSS but 7.3662109375 MiB PSS; shared graphics libraries explain a substantial part of the RSS figure.
conclusion.renderer: KWin reports llvmpipe software rendering. The app maps matching LLVM/Gallium libraries and QtQuick/KF6 integration; its own GL context and original load trigger were not separately identified.
conclusion.comparison: The old long-running guests and the current 44.9648 MiB cold physical Cinnamon workload are different builds, Qt/native stacks and usage histories. This is not a current-build regression comparison or evidence for or against a leak.

verification.processIdentity: Guest PID/startTicks matched supplemental ELF/library reads and dashboard boot/PID/start identity; host QEMU identities matched VNC wall inventory.
verification.counterChecks: All guest smaps categories reconcile to rollup RSS. Source audited: collector VmRSS kB * 1024; UI bytes / 1048576.
verification.review: Separate reused workers inspected dashboard and guest counters, then root checked receipts, scripts, calculations and export hashes. Not a fresh external review.
verification.replayStatus: Guest collector and supplements executed for this observation. Dashboard-only replay helper was prepared from the executed inline GET protocol and syntax-checked; no second live measurement claimed.

limits: Exact running guest source commits and whether each contains unrelated later fixes.
Whether the resident views are currently open or were previously opened, and what actions occurred before sampling.
Which heap pages are live widget/data allocations versus reusable/free allocator pages; smaps does not expose that distinction.
Application GL renderer and the exact trigger for loading QtQuick, LLVM and Gallium; only compositor renderer confirmed.
Fresh same-source/same-workload guest cold, post-view and native-dialog costs; no restart or experiment was authorized/performed.
No physical memory acceptance or fresh-build comparison was rerun.
No guest configuration/history/payload inspected and no inference that all retained heap is reclaimable.
PSS and shared-library mapping attribution explain counters but do not establish causality of all allocation or a leak.
RSS is the retained acceptance metric; PSS is explanatory and does not replace an RSS threshold or establish a pass.
nextStep: For a comparable VM benchmark, use current reviewed source and distro-native packages in fresh disposable overlays; pin identities and separate cold, post-view and post-upload workloads. Retain native dialogs/fonts and VNC. No VM installation or restart performed by this audit.
safety: Only existing-overlay SSH metadata and read-only localhost HTTP were used; VNC stayed available. No graphical acceptance, uploads, captures, credentials, user configuration, payloads, base-disk or app changes.
